title: Raising Up a Generation of Two-Percenters
author: Foster, Michael
summary: Foster argues that parents should aim to raise children who will be among the two percent of their generation who achieve maturity markers early and fully: married, homeowners, and parents by age 25. This is countercultural in an age that celebrates delayed adulthood and endless exploration. Yet the research shows that those who accomplish these things early typically report higher life satisfaction and are insulated from many modern social problems. Foster challenges parents to raise children with intentionality toward these markers, understanding that early adult responsibility and commitment often produce flourishing rather than constraint.
points: Children who become married, homeowners, and parents by 25 are in the top two percent of their generation.
Early achievement of adult markers predicts higher life satisfaction and resilience.
Parental intentionality toward these markers is radical in modern culture.
The two-percent vision offers an alternative to perpetual adolescence and aimlessness.
quotes: Married, homeowner, at least one child, all before 25—these children will be among the two percent.
Early adult responsibility often produces flourishing, not constraint.
Raise your children with the intention of seeing them mature quickly into full adulthood.” Archived from We Made People Substack on May 2, 2026 by Tim.
